# deepsec scan: zerostarter (2026-09-06, fixes 2026-09-06)

Source: [vercel-labs/deepsec](https://github.com/vercel-labs/deepsec) 2.3.9, an agent-powered vulnerability scanner. Its free regex stage (`scan`) picked 165 candidate files with 276 matches; the AI stage (`process`, claude-opus-4-8 at thinking level xhigh, paid through the local Claude Max login rather than an API key) was scoped by manifest to the 59 files that carry the trust boundaries: `api/hono`, `packages/*`, `.github/workflows`, the console and protected routes, and the app's auth and config libs. Marketing, content, OG, docs and error-boundary pages were left out on purpose. Every finding below was re-verified by hand against the source in place of deepsec's paid `revalidate` pass; none was dropped as a false positive. The `.deepsec/` scaffold lives only in the scan worktree and is not committed.

| Stage      | Files | Agent time                            | API-equivalent |
| ---------- | ----- | ------------------------------------- | -------------- |
| Smoke test | 1     | 4 min                                 | $1.64          |
| Scoped run | 58    | 74 min agent, ~30 min wall, 3 workers | $22.84         |

## Findings

deepsec rated nothing CRITICAL or HIGH: 9 MEDIUM and 3 BUG. The auth and console surface (role ladder, middlewares, allowlist, batch writes, console pages, session proxying: thirty files) produced zero findings.

| #   | Finding                                                                             | Where                                            | deepsec         | Verdict                   |
| --- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | --------------- | ------------------------- |
| 1   | Crafted `.gitpickignore` deletes outside the project root on in-place convert       | `packages/cli/src/convert.ts` removeForkExcludes | MEDIUM / medium | Shipped                   |
| 2   | Project name interpolated unescaped into the generated `site.ts`                    | `packages/cli/src/templates.ts` siteTemplate     | MEDIUM / medium | Shipped                   |
| 3   | Rate-limit key trusts client forwarding headers and falls back to a random key      | `api/hono/src/middlewares/rate-limiter.ts`       | MEDIUM / high   | Shipped                   |
| 4   | `/release` comment builds and publishes a PR-selected commit with no origin check   | `.github/workflows/cli-release.yml`              | MEDIUM / low    | Shipped                   |
| 5   | Top-level `id-token: write` and write scopes apply to the test job too              | `.github/workflows/cli-release.yml`              | MEDIUM / low    | Shipped                   |
| 6   | Fork PR file paths mint arbitrary `@<dir>` labels under `pull_request_target`       | `.github/workflows/auto-labeler.yml`             | MEDIUM / medium | Shipped                   |
| 7   | Brand name passed as a `replaceAll` replacement string, so `$` sequences expand     | `packages/cli/src/skills.ts` reconcile           | BUG / medium    | Shipped                   |
| 8   | `action in ACTION_LABELS` walks the prototype chain                                 | `web/next/src/lib/activity.ts` actionLabel       | BUG / low       | Shipped                   |
| 9   | Docker host rewrite replaces the first `localhost` anywhere in `POSTGRES_URL`       | `packages/env/src/db.ts`                         | BUG / low       | Shipped                   |
| 10  | Version and tag strings shell-interpolated into `bun -e` and `bunx json -e`         | `.github/workflows/auto-release.yml`             | MEDIUM / low    | Hardening, inputs trusted |
| 11  | Third-party actions on mutable major tags in token-bearing workflows (two findings) | `auto-labeler.yml`, `cli-release.yml`            | MEDIUM / low    | Decide                    |
| 12  | Public `/og` renders a PNG per distinct query string with no rate limit             | `web/next/src/app/og/route.tsx`                  | MEDIUM / low    | Accept                    |

### Shipped

One commit each on the audit's own PR, with tests under `tests/` mirroring every source file touched.

1. **Exclude containment.** `removeForkExcludes` only rejected glob characters and `parseForkLayout` returns entries verbatim, so `..` climbed out of the root and `.` named the root itself, and an in-place `zerostarter init` inside an untrusted checkout deleted with the user's privileges. Every entry is now resolved and must sit strictly under the root; `.`, `..`, absolute and empty entries fail loudly like the glob check.
2. **Escaped name.** `siteTemplate` wrote `name: "${display}"` and the description line from the directory basename or the prompt answer, so a quote yielded invalid TypeScript and, in a pipeline fed an untrusted name, code at build time. Both literals are emitted with `JSON.stringify`; the README interpolation is markdown and needed nothing.
3. **Anchored rate-limit key.** `findIp` was called with no `platform` or `proxies`, so it read `x-forwarded-for` straight from the request, and an unknown address fell back to a fresh `randomUUIDv7()` per request, which never accumulated. It now receives the peer Bun accepted the connection from: a public peer is the client and no header overrides it, a private peer defers to the `x-forwarded-for` it received, read last hop first, which is what production keyed on all along (Vercel overwrites it with the client: verified on the production API directly and through the zerostarter.dev `/api` rewrite, and on the preview API directly), and a private peer that forwarded nothing is internal traffic (the web app's server-side calls, a health check, local dev behind portless) and is skipped rather than pooled into one bucket that would throttle every user at once. Unattributable requests share one bucket. The durable store stays tracked in the hardening-refactors plan; `manage/rate-limiting.mdx` documents the new resolution.
4. **PR origin asserted before `/release`.** The comment path fetches the PR, requires `head.repo.full_name` to be this repository before checking out its head, and installs with `--ignore-scripts` while the npm token is in the environment. Event values reach the script through `env:`.
5. **Scoped permissions.** The publish scopes moved from the workflow level to the `release` job; the test matrix runs with `contents: read`.
6. **Bounded labels.** A directory label is minted only for a top-level directory that exists on the base checkout; any other path falls back to `@misc`.
7. **Literal replacement.** `replaceAll("ZeroStarter", name)` became a replacer function, so `$&` and friends in a name are text.
8. **Own-property check.** `actionLabel` uses `Object.hasOwn`, as `@packages/auth/access` already did for the same reason.
9. **Host-only rewrite.** A `dockerHostUrl` helper parses the URL and swaps `hostname` alone, so a `localhost` inside the password or the database name stays put.

### Observed while verifying

13. **The public-suffix `/api` rewrite shares a bucket.** From a `*.vercel.app` web host (the preview), the browser reaches the API through the web's `/api` rewrite, and the API then bills a bucket that is not the client's: the same request through the zerostarter.dev rewrite lands in the client's own bucket. Observed against the production API (pre-PR code), so it is pre-existing, not introduced here: the last forwarded address on that path is a Vercel hop. It only affects public-suffix hosts, where every browser call takes the rewrite; a custom domain calls the API directly. The web's server-side session reads on Vercel key on whatever Vercel stamps for a function-to-function call, which is unverified either way. Parked without a verdict: an echo route on a preview API would settle both.

### Hardening, inputs trusted

10. The changelog step interpolates `$MANUAL_VERSION` (from canary's `package.json`) and `$LAST_VERSION` (from the repo's own `v*` tags) into inline script bodies. Both come from reviewed commits and write-access actors, so this is not reachable today. Passing them through `env:` and validating against a semver pattern is cheap and belongs with the workflow-tooling-consistency plan.

### Decide

11. Official actions (`actions/checkout@v6`, `actions/github-script@v8`, `actions/setup-node@v6`) and `oven-sh/setup-bun@v2` ride mutable major tags in the two workflows that hold write tokens and the npm publish. Pinning to commit SHAs with Dependabot for Actions is the standard mitigation; it is a policy choice for the repo rather than a defect, so it is recorded here without a verdict. If declined, note it in the workflow-tooling-consistency plan so the next audit does not re-raise it.

### Accept

12. `/og` is `force-dynamic`, public by nature (social crawlers fetch it unauthenticated), caps every parameter, and is cache-served per URL. The residual risk is cost amplification from many distinct query strings. A coarse per-IP limit would close it, but a rate limiter in the web app is new machinery for a low-confidence finding. Accepted as is; revisit if the OG route ever moves behind the API's limiter for free.

## Scanner notes

- The regex stage is only a file picker and is noisy: 116 of its 119 "insecure-crypto" hits are the letters `des` inside `desc` and `describeRoute`, and most "missing-auth" hits are public pages and error boundaries. Findings come from the AI stage alone.
- The AI stage was precise on this scope: twelve findings, all reproducible in source, and none on the surfaces where a false positive would have been most tempting (the role ladder and the console gates).
- Cost is per file investigated, about $1.6 API-equivalent and four agent-minutes each at xhigh. Scoping by manifest, not by the regex candidates, is what kept this run under $25.

## Adoption

Run it as an occasional audit, not as CI. The scaffold is a pnpm workspace with its own 745 MB `node_modules` inside a Bun monorepo, its tracked files would ship to forks unless added to `.gitpickignore`, and the PR-mode Action needs a gateway secret and per-PR spend that the findings above do not justify against the existing gates (bun audit, CodeRabbit, tests and type checks in PR CI). Re-run on the same scope before a release or after a change to the CLI, the API middlewares or the workflows.

To re-run: scaffold with `npx deepsec@2.3.9 init --scaffold-only --yes` in a worktree, `npm install` inside `.deepsec/`, hand-write `deepsec.config.ts` with `defaultAgent: "claude"` and `ai: { mode: "local", provider: "anthropic" }`, fill `data/<id>/INFO.md` with the auth primitives and known false positives, run `scan`, then `process --agent claude --manifest <files.json> --batch-size 5 --concurrency 3`. deepsec passes its child Claude a fixed env allowlist that drops `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, so point `CLAUDE_CODE_EXECUTABLE` at a one-line shell wrapper that exports that variable and execs the real binary, or the child sees a stale login.
